questions.q: Why is the iron and steel industry called a basic industry, and where is it located in India?

answer.text: The iron and steel industry is called a basic, or key, industry because its products, iron and steel, are the raw materials for many other industries. Machinery, tools, vehicles, railways, ships and construction all depend on steel. The growth of this industry therefore drives the growth of the entire manufacturing sector, which is why it is regarded as the backbone of industrial development.

The industry needs bulky raw materials, iron ore, coal and limestone, so plants are located close to their sources to reduce transport costs. In India most steel plants are concentrated on and around the Chotanagpur plateau in the east, which is rich in these materials. The first modern plant was set up by TISCO at Jamshedpur, followed by public sector plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur and Bokaro.

answer: Thus its central role and its location near raw materials make iron and steel a basic industry.
